turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Trend calculation gives the water-coastal stress scenario a 41 percent probability.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal updated its Trend series with this exact probability on November 18, 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It focuses on Baja California Sur facing that water and coastal stress if nothing shifts.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That figure comes directly from the current series on the portal. It shows what is most likely if trends continue unchanged.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This Vision 2050 does not contest that calculation. [pause] It takes the scenario as the risk to mitigate with deliberate action.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction. It aims for proactive and regenerative outcomes on each driver the Trend identifies.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today's episode is Vision 2050.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Listeners might ask themselves what proactive steps could look like in their own communities. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We will explore that without turning the vision into a forecast of any kind.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Targets stay labelled as aspirations only. No new 2050 numbers get invented where the series stays short.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The concrete question we will answer is how each driver and ceiling can shift toward a proactive and regenerative path for Baja California Sur.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would it take to move the needle on that water and coastal stress risk? [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CONAGUA data from 2023 shows 22 of the 39 aquifers in Baja California Sur sit in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That shortfall totals 105.1 cubic hectometres per year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The constraint shapes every path forward.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes a state where new growth stops drawing from those same deficit aquifers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is presented as a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Only three in ten residents currently have constant supply, according to ENCIG 2025 figures reported locally.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The vision calls for continuous supply to become the rule rather than the exception.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Reuse would add real margin instead of remaining an afterthought.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One lever already under construction is the second Cabo San Lucas desal plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is slated to reach 250 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That would bring the combined output to 655 litres per second by 2027.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The plant is described as a supply addition, not a reason to keep extracting from overdrawn aquifers. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another step is closing the 25 documented illegal taps in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The estimated 300 litres per second they divert should reach users instead.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Growth permits would tie directly to mean annual availability per aquifer under NOM-011.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Offsets that only exist on paper would no longer count.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's demand-supply board prevents one municipality's deficit from being masked by headroom elsewhere.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That brings us to the coast. UABCS measurements during El Niño record wave-height increases of 15 to 30 centimetres at Puerto San Carlos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal notes that surge, erosion and flooding are already visible along developed shorelines.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its Vision 2050 describes a habitable, regenerative coast where restoring barriers and beaches, and retreating from risk zones, come before any new occupation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No modelled 2050 shoreline position is offered, because comparable long-term data do not yet exist.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One concrete action is completing the environmental reviews already opened, such as the case of Hotel San Cristóbal at Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The goal is to avoid leaving debris and precedent that future surges could simply wash away.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Relocation and retreat would be placed at the front of decisions rather than treated as an after-the-fact remedy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Respect for ANP boundaries and coastal-planning limits would also precede any further hospitality scaling in East Cape, Loreto or the Pacific corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal frames these steps as necessary to keep the coast both livable and productive. [chuckle] What part of the water or coastal picture would you want to examine first if you were setting priorities?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The state economy grew 3.5 percent in constant prices in 2024, according to INEGI.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That puts the total at 187,152 million pesos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. Tourism numbers still cluster in one corridor though.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: SETUE data show Los Cabos at 70.0 percent occupancy for 2025.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz sat at 64 percent the same year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Hotel Association later recorded 78 percent occupancy in Los Cabos for the first half of November 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That jump stands out.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: FDI reached 1,353 million dollars in 2024, per CNIE figures.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It rose to 1,578 million the next year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Formal employment posted a 1.1 percent year-on-year drop in October.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: There were 224,460 IMSS posts counted in September.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes a desirable, achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It calls for tourism that stays inside measured water, energy and coastal limits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Instead of repeating the same coastal model everywhere. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Occupancy and visitor spending would serve as signals, not as volume targets for 2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same vision sees a polycentric economy where investment spreads beyond one corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Paz would act as the services and infrastructure node.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú could focus on agriculture with more room, and the north on energy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One lever would condition any new tourism or residential project on proven water and power margins.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without relying on uncredited supply. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Another treats beach closures or coastal quality drops as hard limits on the vocation itself.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A third lever shifts relative weight toward La Paz, Loreto and the interior.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each with its own role rather than scaled-down copies of the same model.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For the economy, the vision would weigh formal employment and inflation together with the same water and grid ceilings.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It would not treat outside forum goals, such as tripling FDI, as already accepted projections.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That keeps the focus on what can actually be supported without overloading the existing systems.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The levers are presented as choices the state could still make, not as outcomes already in motion.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Tourism news items reached eight in the period, with an EWMA of 7.70 and neutral direction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Economy items were three, at an EWMA of 5.79, also neutral.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The vision would read those employment figures alongside the water and grid limits from the start.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So any growth plan would first check actual supply margins instead of assuming they appear later.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That approach avoids locking the state into one corridor when other regions still have headroom.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you watch first if these levers were tested in the next budget cycle?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: BCS power data shows the island grid still caps at one ceiling. SIBCS hit 689 MW peak in 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That single limit keeps shaping everything else.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal records 660 MW net for 2023.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And 675 MW the same year. Tourism growth and desalination both draw from the same lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Energy items stayed flat this week, EWMA at 1.66 with no clear direction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the mobility side, SJD traffic fell 4.6 percent in October.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And 5.5 percent for the year to date.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: LAP rose 8.7 percent year-to-date, according to GAP 2026 figures.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Three mobility items appeared this week, EWMA 2.67, still mixed.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes a system that leaves island-grid limits behind through clean generation and storage sized to the real SIBCS ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: For mobility, the same vision sees connectivity serving a polycentric state instead of feeding only the SJD–Los Cabos corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: LAP already functions as one measured counterweight.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One lever is finishing the remote-generation tenders already visible in the north, kept transparent and not turned into residential permits ahead of time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A second is planning desalination and pumping together with the grid instead of adding them later as extra megawatts.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Demand from new tourism or real estate in Cabos would only move forward once SIBCS margin is shown.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For air and sea links, the vision keeps LAP traffic and Sea of Cortez ferries as working alternatives for freight and passengers where projects already exist.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Paving and traffic counts would serve communities first, not only new coastal projects.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That keeps growth from concentrating where the grid and runways are already tight.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What remains uncertain is exactly how quickly storage can close the island gap.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The levers stay practical because they start from numbers already published.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: If tenders finish on schedule, remote supply could ease the single ceiling without new local plants.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And if LAP keeps its measured growth, it spreads pressure away from SJD.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 therefore treats both pillars as design choices rather than fixed limits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: November 18, 2026 marks the date these figures were reviewed for the vision.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. That date lines up with the latest GAP and SIBCS records.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One more practical point: the vision treats the 2024 peak as the benchmark that future storage must respect.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. No added demand moves forward without that margin shown first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [chuckle] It keeps the plan grounded in what the grid can actually carry today.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you watch first, the next tender round or the LAP numbers?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 opens with a documented risk for housing.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: State population stood at 798,447 according to the INEGI Census 2020.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That number sets the scale for what comes next.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Housing grows exposed when it appears in places without services or in coastal and water-risk zones.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Housing accounts for one item this week with an EWMA of 1.81.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That exposure is the starting point the vision wants to change [chuckle].

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes housing with services, set off the first line of risk, and aligned with real water and energy margins.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No 2050 housing-unit target is published, so the vision stays within the evidence already held.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One lever is to prioritise relocating what is already exposed before opening a new residential front on the coast or on aquifers in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That makes sense as a first step.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Another is to cross-check every development with the demand-supply board and with current planning instruments.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Treat backlog and the lack of services as a ceiling, not as a gap the market will close on its own.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Now the governance pillar carries two items this week with an EWMA of 3.57 and a direction of plus 0.50.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without instruments that bind growth to measured ceilings, the current path wins by the inertia of permits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes public decisions that make POEL, PDU, PMDU, consultations and ANP ceilings prior conditions, not paperwork after the fact.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It remains achievable only if those instruments are used with the evidence the portal already holds.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One lever is to close already marked gaps with evidence in Loreto and the northern DMA before larger public scenarios.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Keep public consultation and the delivery of instruments to Congress as visible levers, not as closing paperwork.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Use the state's constrained board reading as a permit criterion, not only as an analysis text.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That approach turns measured ceilings into actual permit rules.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the full set of levers the vision offers for both pillars.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The approach stays grounded in what is already measured.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And it treats the instruments as binding tools rather than optional steps [pause].

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the planning offices next?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes five conditions that must be true for the future it describes to become real in Baja California Sur.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. That frame matters right away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For instance, tourism in Los Cabos would look different from production up north in every planning document.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right, and that protects the unique character of places like Loreto and the East Cape coast.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The first condition is that each vocation contributes a distinct role.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Not diluted into a single statewide version of Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That keeps the character of different regions intact.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about how that plays out on the ground.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The second condition concerns new tourism and residential growth.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It can only happen where water and energy show clear margin or come from a non-DMA source such as desalination.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without pretending to use NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That prevents overcommitment of resources that are not there. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The evidence requirement for those gaps in the north could delay some projects by years according to the portal.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet it avoids the shortages we have seen elsewhere. What would you ask the water authority about the DMA?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Third, East Cape and Loreto must respect ANP and POEL ceilings before any scaling of hospitality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The limits stay in place even when demand rises.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. You cannot assume the ceilings will stretch later.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fourth, Comondú and the north can add production and energy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But only without emptying local services or protected natural areas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The fifth condition addresses marked gaps.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto and north DMA shortfalls, amenity rooms, the Cabos PDU, and pumping megawatts must be closed with evidence first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Before any public scenario moves forward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: These steps together keep the vision grounded in what the region can actually support.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each one protects a different part of the system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stands out is how they tie local data to any next step.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The conditions force evidence before growth claims are accepted.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: These conditions seem practical once you map them to actual sites across the municipalities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They do. I wonder how residents in Comondú see the balance with new energy projects.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's Vision 2050 proposes a set of practical levers for Baja California Sur.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Some already show movement on the ground, while others remain proposals that would need clear action from state agencies and municipalities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Take the second desal plant in Cabo San Lucas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It sits at 75 percent completion right now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That would add 250 liters per second once finished.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Combined that reaches 655 liters per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The target date is 2027.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That counts as a supply lever already under construction.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The vision stresses it cannot serve as a licence to keep drawing from aquifers already in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Other water levers focus on closing illegal taps.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They also call for tying growth permits to mean annual availability under NOM-011.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal wants its demand-supply board used so one municipality's deficit is not offset on paper elsewhere.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This remains a desirable and achievable future, not a prediction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: For the coast, the vision points to finishing environmental reviews already opened.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One example is the review for Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It places relocation and retreat at the front of decisions.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That would require municipalities to act before any new permits move forward.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tourism levers would condition new growth on evidenced water and power margin.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They also push to shift weight toward La Paz, Loreto and the interior.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: In energy, the proposals call for completing remote-generation tenders visible in the north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those tenders should not turn into residential permits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mobility levers would hold up the La Paz airport node as a counterweight to Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That uses published GAP figures.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Housing would prioritise relocating exposed structures before opening new coastal fronts.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Governance levers would close documented gaps in places like Loreto and northern DMA first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The vision keeps public consultation visible rather than paperwork at the end.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly, so agencies can use the constrained board reading as an actual permit criterion.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you want to see measured first before any of these levers advance?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Right, Luz. That vision focuses on steady progress in places like La Paz and Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. It shows how careful planning today could give families here more stable jobs and cleaner water supplies later.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait, Luz— that last point on water really stands out to me.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does, because the vision ties those supplies directly to daily routines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And that matters because people in BCS would feel the difference in daily life, from how they work to how they get around.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] It keeps things practical, the way we like it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's vision proposes better connections between towns and stronger local institutions to handle growth.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, and that could mean fewer surprises when the next dry season hits or when tourism shifts.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. I keep thinking about how those institutions would actually work on the ground.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They would let towns share resources instead of each one solving problems alone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So what changes for people is simply more room to plan ahead instead of reacting all the time.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you change first in your own neighborhood to match that kind of future?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And how might your town look if the vision's ideas took hold step by step?
